messages:
tara: Quick RFC follow-up: we need to pick a migration adapter approach for v2 clients. Two options on the table: in-path facade (runtime-integrated) vs sidecar shim. Thoughts on latency, operability, and rollback complexity?

mattg: Sidecar for me. Keeps runtime cleaner and lets infra iterate independently. Downsides: extra hop, more scheduling.

ciara: Sidecar hop adds p95. On host-local loopback ~1-2ms, but on k8s NodePort it can grow. Are we comfortable adding that to our 50ms p95 SLO for simple generate?

tara: 50ms p95 is current. +1-3ms seems OK but we should profile short prompts where every ms counts.

ben: Facade-in-path wins for tracing simplicity and fewer moving parts. Sidecar needs cross-process tracing and more tag plumbing.

sam: Proposal: hybrid model. Lightweight facade for hot-path trivial transforms (header mapping, small encoding fixes). Full sidecar for complex rewrites (stream framing, multipart->ndjson).

ciara: Hybrid is pragmatic. How to decide routing? Header from client? request size? capability probe?

tara: Recommend capability handshake: clients attach `X-RW-Client-Version`. Runtime exposes `X-RW-Compat` capability. Facade inspects mismatch and, for heavy cases, proxies to sidecar.

olivia: Note: v2 renames auth header in some tenants. Facade must preserve token semantics and never log raw tokens. Must be in-memory only.

ben: Example header shim (pseudocode):

```
// facade middleware
if (req.headers["Authorization"] && !req.headers["X-RW-Auth"]) {
  req.headers["X-RW-Auth"] = req.headers["Authorization"]
  delete req.headers["Authorization"]
}
```

ciara: Scrub sensitive fields in traces: set `otel.attribute.credentials_present=true`, do not record token strings.

mattg: Rollout plan: 1) tenant opt-in flag, 2) staged default for new tenants, 3) after 8 weeks flip for all with opt-out window. Track error rates and latency deltas.

sam: Streaming chunk reframe is tricky. Facade can handle trivial wrapper changes, but for ndjson <-> SSE reframe we should prefer sidecar.

tara: Add runtime config to prefer local translation when CPU <= 70% and p95 delta < 5%. Prevents overload on busy nodes.

olivia: Private deployments: KMS/HSM flows require passthrough semantics. Facade must not terminate KMS TLS; sidecar needs support for TLS passthrough to customer KMS. Document for Private customers.

ben: Observability metrics to add: `compat.facade.latency_ms`, `compat.sidecar.proxy_count`, `compat.translated_requests_total`. Tag by `tenant_id`, `model_family`, `reason_code`.

ciara: I'll run load/perf tests (10k prompt variations) to compare facade vs sidecar. ETA 3 days.

mattg: Agreed TL;DR: hybrid. Facade for trivial transforms & handshake; sidecar for heavy protocol rewrites and KMS passthrough. Feature flags + tracing scrub + telemetry. Rollout: opt-in -> staged default -> full flip after metrics look healthy.

tara: Action list:
- ciara: perf/load tests (3d)
- ben: telemetry + tracing scrub design (2d)
- olivia: Private KMS passthrough doc (3d)
- mattg: sidecar resource + dev plan (4d)
- sam: facade lightweight impl PR (2d)

infra-bot: deploy-checklist: add canary pool `compat-adapter`, circuit-breaker default 10qps, health endpoint `/compat/health`.

tara: I'll update the RFC with this hybrid plan and the action items. Will re-ping after tests. :thumbsup:
